title: AP Precalculus 3.1 — Periodic Phenomena
question: Periodic patterns: find a period, a midline and an amplitude, predict later values, and read where a graph falls.
intro:
**Quick recap:**

\[
\begin{aligned}
f(x+P) &= f(x) \\
\text{midline} &= \frac{\max+\min}{2} \\
\text{amplitude} &= \frac{\max-\min}{2}
\end{aligned}
\]

- The period \(P\) is the length of one full cycle.
- To predict a later value, take away whole periods first.

**Show your calculation before choosing A–D.**

questions.title: Find the period
questions.prompt:
A function takes these values at \(x=0,1,2,3,\dots\)

\[
0,\ 2,\ 2,\ 0,\ -2,\ -2,\ 0,\ 2,\ 2,\ 0,\ -2,\ -2,\ \dots
\]

What is its period?
questions.solution_title: Find where the whole pattern starts again
questions.solution:
- One full cycle: \(0,\ 2,\ 2,\ 0,\ -2,\ -2\), then it starts again.

\[
\begin{aligned}
f(x+6) &= f(x)
\end{aligned}
\]

\[
\boxed{P=6}
\]

- Not \(3\): \(0\) comes back after \(3\) steps, but then the values go down, not up.
- Not \(2\) or \(4\): \(f(2)=2\) but \(f(4)=-2\); the pattern does not repeat there.

questions.title: Midline and amplitude
questions.prompt: On a summer day in Valletta the temperature goes up to \(31^\circ\text{C}\) in the afternoon and down to \(23^\circ\text{C}\) at night, day after day. Which pair is correct?
questions.solution_title: Average for the midline, half the range for the amplitude
questions.solution:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{midline} &= \frac{31+23}{2} \\
&= 27 \\
\text{amplitude} &= \frac{31-23}{2} \\
&= 4
\end{aligned}
\]

\[
\boxed{27\,^\circ\text{C and }4\,^\circ\text{C}}
\]

- Not amplitude \(8\): that is \(\max-\min\); the amplitude is half of it.
- Not midline \(4\) or \(8\): the midline is a temperature level between \(23\) and \(31\).

questions.title: Predict with the period
questions.prompt: A periodic function \(f\) has period \(5\) and \(f(2)=7\). What is \(f(17)\)?
questions.solution:
\[
\begin{aligned}
17-3\cdot5 &= 2 \\
f(17) &= f(2) \\
&= 7
\end{aligned}
\]

\[
\boxed{f(17)=7}
\]

- Not \(17\) or \(2\): those are inputs, not outputs.
- Not \(35\): \(7\cdot5\); the period moves the input, it never multiplies the output.

questions.title: A Ferris wheel later
questions.prompt: A Ferris wheel has diameter \(30\) m and its centre is \(18\) m above the ground. It turns once every \(10\) minutes. A seat is at the bottom (\(3\) m) at \(t=0\). How high is the seat at \(t=25\) minutes?
questions.solution_title: Back to the first turn, then half a turn
questions.solution:
\[
\begin{aligned}
25-2\cdot10 &= 5 \\
h(25) &= h(5)
\end{aligned}
\]

- \(t=5\) is half a turn after the bottom: the top.

\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{top} &= 18+15 \\
&= 33
\end{aligned}
\]

\[
\boxed{33\text{ m}}
\]

- Not \(3\) m: that is the bottom, at \(t=0,\ 10,\ 20,\ 30\).
- Not \(18\) m: the centre height is passed at \(t=2.5\) and \(7.5\) in each turn.
- Not \(25\) m: the time is not the height.

questions.title: Where is it decreasing?
questions.prompt: The figure shows a periodic function \(g\) with high points \((2,\,3)\) and \((10,\,3)\) and a low point \((6,\,-1)\). On which interval is \(g\) **decreasing**?
questions.figure_alt: A periodic wave from x = -2 to 12: high points (2, 3) and (10, 3), low point (6, -1)
questions.solution_title: High point to the next low point
questions.solution:
- From the high point at \(x=2\) down to the low point at \(x=6\), \(g\) falls the whole time.

\[
\boxed{2<x<6}
\]

- Not \(-2<x<2\) or \(6<x<10\): low to high, so \(g\) is increasing.
- Not \(0<x<4\): \(g\) rises until \(x=2\), then falls. Mixed.

takeaway: One full cycle tells you everything: period, midline, amplitude, and every later value.
